shelter noun

Traupman 298

suffugium, suffugiī n.

noun, second declension · Declension on Wiktionary

a shelter (from rain, cold, sun)

A place one runs under for cover: post-Augustan (Seneca, Pliny, Tacitus). Also, figuratively, a remedy or way out.

Other words

  • perfugium, perfugiī n. — a refuge, a place to flee to

    noun, second declension · also used · classical · Caes. BG 4.38 (Lewis & Short); Cic. Div. 2.150: perfugium omnium labōrum et sollicitūdinum somnus (Lewis & Short) · Declension on Wiktionary

    Refuge from danger or trouble, a safe haven; the classical word of Plautus, Caesar and Cicero.

  • tēctum, tēctī n. — a roof; a roof over one’s head

    noun, second declension · also used · classical · Declension on Wiktionary

    Shelter as a building: tēctō recipere (Cic.), to give someone shelter; sub tēctum, under cover (see roof). The ē is long by Lachmann’s law (tegō).

Examples

  • nec aliud īnfantibus ferārum imbriumque suffugium quam ut in aliquō rāmōrum nexū contegantur

    their babies have no other shelter from wild beasts and rain than to be covered over in a tangle of branchesTac. Germ. 46.4

  • Pluit: sub porticū suffugium petāmus.

    It’s raining: let’s take shelter under the porch.composed

See also protect, roof, hide.
